analysis: Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift head 1838-2182 (unchanged context: sweepExpiredEntries, scanOnDisk symlink/safe-root checks, settleDurableDonation re-read and binding validation, performIndexedRemoval ownsEvictionRoot gate) plus the file_changes patch for evictOldestEntry (head ~1769-1777). The change replaces the inline loop over index.oldestEntries() with SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) calling retireIndexedEntries per tag. The evictions stat is incremented once when freed > 0, which matches the previous behavior. The SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot implementations are not in this batch. The new tests specify the contract: return 0 when externalChange occurs, including in the fallback (SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests head 117-142); skip busy or undeletable files (84-115); leave files untouched when the epoch is refused (187-196); keep the fallback snapshot bounded and frozen against concurrent touch/insert (198-247); and keep a deterministic unsigned tie-break order (SSDBlockIndexTests 31-88). Relative to T-041, the LRU disk budget, TTL, HMAC naming, safe-root/symlink guards and epoch behavior appear preserved, assuming the helper meets this test contract. A box-wide budget that fails to evict would be an availability/disk issue (T-016), not a disclosure issue. Integration must verify that SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest stops on externalChange, terminates on an all-busy index (no unbounded loop or restart), and does not call the callback while holding the index lock. It must also confirm that retireIndexedEntries still routes through performIndexedRemoval/ownsEvictionRoot and the safe-path removal. No regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
